html:
The leader of the Union of the Peoples of Cameroon (UPC), the first party to demand full independence and the reunification of the French and British parts of Cameroon.

He argued Cameroon's case at the United Nations in the 1950s. France banned the UPC in 1955, and it took up arms in the forests of Sanaga-Maritime and later the Bamileke highlands. French troops killed Um Nyobe in the bush on 13 September 1958. The war went on into the 1960s under Ahidjo, with tens of thousands killed, and its history was banned for decades. In 2025 France formally acknowledged that it had waged a war there. His name was only rehabilitated in Cameroon in 1991.
